text:
GitHub Copilot Fusion became generally available Oct 28, bringing automatic model routing and multi-model workflows. Try Fusion Standard on one small bug, with a reproducible test and a diff review: model orchestration is a workflow, not proof of correctness.
Follow @layer8culture if you're building with AI.

Copilot Fusion: a 15-minute experiment before you change your AI stack.

What changed: GitHub made Fusion generally available Oct 28. Instead of choosing a specific model, you select Fusion and an effort level.

What it does: routes work across enabled models, using Single, Cascade or Critique workflows when appropriate. Critique means draft, review, revise. It isn't a substitute for your own tests.

Builder value: less manual model switching; more room to define the task and inspect the result. Standard targets everyday coding, High targets challenging work, and Max targets the most demanding work. More effort isn't automatically the right choice.

Try this week: in a scratch branch, choose one tiny bug and write the failing behavior first. Run Fusion Standard, review the diff, then run the test. Record correctness, elapsed time and reported usage or cost. Compare with your usual setup on the same starting code, not a vague memory.

Fusion bills for each model it uses. Check your plan and usage; don't assume routing means free work.

The bigger signal: model choice is becoming workflow orchestration. Your acceptance criteria still belong to you.

Save this for your next AI stack decision.
